exposure: mother's use of over-the-counter (OTC) medications during pregnancy
intake of any medication throughout pregnancy
taking paracetamol once per week during pregnancy
proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) once per month
cohort: The study involved 1000 Lebanese students aged between 4 and 17 years from both public and private schools.
finding: The intake of any medication during pregnancy, weekly paracetamol use, and monthly PPI use during pregnancy were significantly associated with higher odds of asthma in children, while breastfeeding was associated with lower odds of asthma.
